def test_the_version_moves_when_any_part_of_the_contract_moves():
        """The gate that stops `CONTRACT_VERSION` becoming a number nobody maintains.
    
        A failure here is not a defect. It means something crossing the boundary changed, which is
        allowed and expected -- and the contract has to SAY so, because a client compares the number
        before it compares anything else. Bump the version, paste the new digest above, and the two
        facts stay attached to each other.
        """
        live = C.digests()
        moved = {name: (PINNED[name], live[name]) for name in PINNED if PINNED[name] != live[name]}
        added = sorted(set(live) - set(PINNED))
        if moved or added:

d.name: James Cameron
d.notes:
The camera is mounted and travelling — it rides with the body or the machine rather than observing them, and it finishes a move on a different part of the space from the one it started on. Reach first for Tracking Shot, Push In, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pull Out, Arc Shot, Pedestal Up, Pedestal Down and Shake Strongly; leave Static Shot and the rolls alone.
Frame wide enough that the space and the hardware in it read as large against the person, and tighten onto a face only at the moment a decision gets made. Low angles, letting a structure loom over whoever is under it.
Light with hard sources that exist inside the frame — work lamps, flares, screens, fire — carving figures out of a cold cyan-blue ambient, with atmosphere thick enough that a beam has a shape in the air, and one warm amber source somewhere against the blue.
Spend the description on the mechanism: what a thing is made of, what is bolted to what, the readout, the water, the load a surface is taking. Then the face, at the point where the person decides.
Bodies show competence under load. They brace, grip, take weight and keep working, and the effort shows in the hands and the jaw before it reaches the voice. Delivery is clipped, functional, and pitched slightly too loud for the room.
The room is close mechanical detail over a low pressurised bed — servo, hydraulic, metal under stress, water moving as mass — with its own hum continuing underneath all of it. The music is full orchestra with one solo instrument carrying the line above it, percussion entering under the movement, a wide dynamic range, building across a long sustained rise instead of arriving already loud.

d.name: Quentin Tarantino
d.notes:
The camera sits still and keeps holding after the action in the shot has finished. When it does move it starts abruptly, travels fast and stops dead instead of easing out. Reach first for Static Shot, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Tilt Down and POV; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals and the shakes alone.
Frame flat and frontal while people talk, from a lens height that is either eye level or startlingly low, looking up from below the tabletop. An insert is enormous relative to the thing it shows.
Light from ordinary sources — daylight through a window, tungsten in a room, the flat fluorescent of a public interior — but the colour off them is rich and heavily saturated: deep reds, hot yellows, warm browns, blacks that stay warm. Surfaces are worn, greasy and used, lit so the wear reads as colour rather than as grime.
Point the camera at hands, feet and footwear, the object on the table, what somebody is eating, the thing being carried, the boot of a car — and a face kept in frame after it has stopped speaking.
People talk at length about small unrelated things, relaxed and unhurried, then stop mid-thought and change tone inside a single beat. Delivery is easy and conversational until it drops flat and quiet.
The room is dry and close — a chair on a hard floor, cutlery, a hard-soled step, the exact mechanical sound an object makes as it is picked up and set down, very little air in it. The music is source-flavoured rather than orchestral: reverb-heavy surf guitar, a soul rhythm section, spaghetti-western brass, an isolated whistled line, holding one tempo and one volume from start to finish with no swell under the action.

d.name: Wes Anderson
d.notes:
The camera sits dead centre and moves only along a rigid axis — a fast flat pivot to the next arrangement, a straight lateral, or a straight advance. It never curves and never comes off the horizontal. Reach first for Static Shot, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Zoom In, Tilt Down and Push In; leave Arc Shot, Tracking Shot, the shakes, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame in one-point perspective, perfectly symmetrical, the subject centred and square to the lens looking very nearly down the barrel. An insert is a flat overhead plan view of objects laid out in a row.
Light evenly and almost shadowlessly, high key, with no source doing anything dramatic. A small closed palette of related saturated colours — buttery yellows, pinks, faded reds, sage — against a pale ground.
Point the camera at things that were arranged on purpose: labelled objects, printed matter, the contents of a container, a hand presenting an item flat to the lens, an itemised row of possessions.
Performance is deadpan and upright. Bodies are held square and still, heads turn on the horizontal, and feeling is said out loud instead of shown. Delivery is flat and quick, evenly paced, with no emphasis on any word.
The room is clean and slightly stylised — a small number of specific isolated sounds, each one distinct, over a quiet and almost neutral room tone. The music is plucked strings, harpsichord or celesta playing a brisk repeated figure at a fixed tempo held steady throughout, or one unaccompanied acoustic guitar.

d.name: Denis Villeneuve
d.notes:
The camera stays still for a long time, and when it moves it travels in one continuous motion at a constant slow rate from the start of the move to the end of it. Reach first for Static Shot, Push In, Pull Out, Pedestal Up, Pedestal Down, Tilt Up, Arc Shot and Tracking Shot; leave the zooms, the shakes, the rolls and the pans alone.
Frame the extreme wide where a figure is a small mark against the mass of the thing behind it, cut against a face filling the frame with nothing legible behind it. Nothing in the middle.
Light with one hard directional source through a great deal of atmosphere — dust, fog, particulate — so the light has volume. Reduce the frame nearly to a single hue at a time, ochre or slate or near-black, and let figures go to silhouette against a bright void.
Spend the description on mass and scale — the surface of a structure, the distance to a horizon, how much empty space surrounds a body — and then a face, small in the frame, with the rest of the frame empty.
Performance is withheld. Bodies move slowly and deliberately, hold still for a long time before acting, and give almost nothing away. Delivery is quiet, low and unhurried, often barely above the room.
The room is enormous low-frequency air: wind across open ground, a long decay on every impact, and real near-silence between events rather than a bed filling the gaps. The music is a sustained low drone with brass swelling out of it at a very slow tempo and no discernible melody, instruments added one at a time, the volume rising continuously to the end.

d.name: Kathryn Bigelow
d.notes:
The camera is carried and reacting rather than planned — it finds the subject a beat late, corrects, and gets jostled by what is happening beside it. It stands among the people in the scene rather than apart from them. Reach first for Shake Slightly, Shake Strongly, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pan Left, Pan Right, Push In and POV; leave Arc Shot, the rolls and Static Shot alone.
Frame on a long lens from a real distance, so the frame is cropped tight and partly blocked by whatever sits between the camera and the subject. The subject falls wherever it happens to fall, often off-centre and part-cut by the frame edge.
Light with whatever the location actually has and nothing added — flat overcast daylight, dust-bleached sun, one work light, night lit only by what somebody switched on. The colour is drained rather than rich: greys, dust, washed blue-white, no warmth put back anywhere and no source arranged to flatter anything.
Point the camera at procedure: the sequence of actions a trained person performs, equipment being used correctly, hands doing a specific technical job, and the periphery being scanned for what is about to happen.
Performance is professional and unglamorous. People do a job under stress, and effort and fear show as breathing and small errors rather than as expression. Delivery is terse, overlapping and functional.
The room is immediate and unmixed — breathing inside the frame, gear and fabric, sharp transient impacts with no tail, and a background that keeps intruding on the foreground. The music is very quiet and very sparse: one low sustained tone, or a dry percussive pulse at a steady unchanging rate, mixed below the sound of the room.

d.name: Wong Kar-wai
d.notes:
The camera watches from just outside the moment, low and close, drifting slowly sideways past whatever is in the way, and never repositions for a clear view. Reach first for Static Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Push In, Pan Left, Pan Right and Tilt Down; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals, Shake Strongly and the rolls alone.
Frame tight and obstructed — taken through a doorway, a grille, a mirror or the back of someone's head, with a foreground object cutting into a third of the frame and the subject pushed to the edge of it.
Light in saturated practical colour at night: neon and signage bleeding into the air, tungsten pools, jade green and deep red against black, a smear of light around every source and no even fill anywhere.
Point the camera at repeated intimate detail — a cigarette, a clock, a sleeve, steam coming off food, a hand not quite touching another one — and at the small distance between two people who are not looking at each other.
People stand very close together and do not touch. A hand lifts partway and comes back down. Movements start late and finish slowly, and delivery is soft, quiet and aimed slightly away from whoever it was meant for.
The room keeps the intimate layer close and the world muffled behind it — a fan, rain on an awning, distant traffic, crockery in another room, all of it slightly too far away. The music is one instrument carrying a short melody that repeats without developing — solo strings, a plucked guitar, a slow Latin waltz — at a fixed unhurried tempo, the same figure repeating from beginning to end at one volume.

d.name: Steven Spielberg
d.notes:
The camera advances steadily onto whoever is seeing something and keeps advancing after they have registered it — the move ends on a face rather than on the thing that caused it. Reach first for Push In, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pedestal Up, Tilt Up, Arc Shot and Pull Out; leave Shake Strongly, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame at eye level or slightly below, so the world reads at the height of whoever is smallest in the scene. A clean wide that holds the whole group, then a slow tightening onto one reaction inside it.
Light with a strong warm source from behind or beside the subject, throwing a visible shaft through haze or dust, edges rimmed bright, faces lifted by a soft bounce, and the source often flaring straight into the lens.
Point the camera at the reaction rather than the cause — what a face does at the moment it understands, a group turning together, a small object held out on an open palm. The thing itself is frequently kept out of frame.
Performance is readable and unguarded. Wonder, fear and recognition arrive on the face fully and without irony; bodies lean in, reach out, take a step forward. Delivery is warm and overlapping, and people talk over each other.
The room has layered naturalistic depth — the near sound, the middle-distance activity and a real horizon behind them — with the specific sound of the thing being reacted to arriving before it is seen. The music is a full orchestra carrying one clear melodic line on strings or a solo horn, which plays through in full at least once, rises, and lands resolved.

Reach first for Push In, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pedestal Up, Tilt Up, Arc Shot and Pull Out; leave Shake Strongly, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame at eye level or slightly below, so the world reads at the height of whoever is smallest in the scene. A clean wide that holds the whole group, then a slow tightening onto one reaction inside it.
Light with a strong warm source from behind or beside the subject, throwing a visible shaft through haze or dust, edges rimmed bright, faces lifted by a soft bounce, and the source often flaring straight into the lens.
Point the camera at the reaction rather than the cause — what a face does at the moment it understands, a group turning together, a small object held out on an open palm. The thing itself is frequently kept out of frame.
Performance is readable and unguarded. Wonder, fear and recognition arrive on the face fully and without irony; bodies lean in, reach out, take a step forward. Delivery is warm and overlapping, and people talk over each other.
The room has layered naturalistic depth — the near sound, the middle-distance activity and a real horizon behind them — with the specific sound of the thing being reacted to arriving before it is seen. The music is a full orchestra carrying one clear melodic line on strings or a solo horn, which plays through in full at least once, rises, and lands resolved.

def test_a_frame_anchor_is_exempt_from_a_transformation_marker():
        """The exposure check the lead asked for on the preservation-flavoured rules, and it found a real
        contradiction — resolved in the OPPOSITE direction from R15's.
    
        A frame anchor is a conditioning latent that is never denoised, so its own pixels cannot be
        transformed; the transformation applies to the rest of the video. `marker_for_plate` handed
        `attribute_transfer` to every plate including that one, so R6 (an anchor must be fully_preserved)
        and R7 (a Picture cannot transfer) both fired on a perfectly coherent request — "start from this
        frame and reimagine the rest as anime". The compiler contradicted itself and the model could not
        fix it.
    
        R15's collision was fixed by deferring to the REQUEST, because the caller owns wardrobe. This one

def test_a_frame_anchor_is_exempt_from_a_transformation_marker():
        """The exposure check the lead asked for on the preservation-flavoured rules, and it found a real
        contradiction — resolved in the OPPOSITE direction from R15's.
    
        A frame anchor is a conditioning latent that is never denoised, so its own pixels cannot be
        transformed; the transformation applies to the rest of the video. `marker_for_plate` handed
        `attribute_transfer` to every plate including that one, so R6 (an anchor must be fully_preserved)
        and R7 (a Picture cannot transfer) both fired on a perfectly coherent request — "start from this
        frame and reimagine the rest as anime". The compiler contradicted itself and the model could not
        fix it.
    
        R15's collision was fixed by deferring to the REQUEST, because the caller owns wardrobe. This one
        defers to the MECHANISM, because nothing owns a latent that is never denoised. "Who owns the
        attribute" does not always answer "the request".
    
        **§43 makes the exemption moot and keeps this test as the stronger guard.** The collision existed
        only because a transformation overrode the marker at all, and that override was a misreading of
        `attribute_transfer`. With it deleted, NO plate's marker depends on the licence — anchor or not —
        so R6 and R7 can never be tripped by us. Asserted for both roles, which is what the exemption was
        protecting, and it now also fails if anyone re-introduces the override.
        """
        from h3ir.licence import resolve_licence
    
        card = AssetCard(sha256="i1", kind=AssetKind.IMAGE, style="live-action photo",
                         subjects=[{"kind": "person", "descriptor": "the man",
                                    "attributes": ["charcoal technical jacket"]}])
        anchor = AssetRef(kind=AssetKind.IMAGE, role=Role.FRAME_ANCHOR_FIRST, sha256="i1", px=(700, 500))
        brief = Brief(intent="start from this frame and reimagine the whole thing as anime as he walks "
                             "away", seconds=8.0, assets=[anchor])
        lic = resolve_licence(brief, {"i1": card})
    
        assert lic.medium_transferred, "the request IS a transformation"
        assert not hasattr(lic, "marker_for_plate"), (
            "the licence must not decide a retention marker at all — see §43")
        for role in (Role.SUBJECT, Role.FRAME_ANCHOR_FIRST, Role.FRAME_ANCHOR_LAST):
            ref = AssetRef(kind=AssetKind.IMAGE, role=role, sha256="i1", px=(700, 500))
>           plan = deterministic_draft(replace(brief, assets=[ref]), Mode.FL2VA, {"i1": card},
                                       opts=ProfileOptions())

A generous mound of freshly chopped, bright green scallions rests in the center, and a crisp, dark green rectangular sheet of nori seaweed is tucked into the right edge. On the right side of the table, a spherical paper lantern with a ribbed bamboo frame sits on a black wooden base. Behind them, traditional Japanese sliding shoji screens with wooden lattice frames are open, revealing a bright outdoor scene with lush green trees. Early in the clip, the thick, white steam rising from the hot ramen broth immediately intensifies, billowing upwards in thick, swirling clouds that dance continuously above the bowl. As the clip progresses into the middle seconds, the camera maintains its static position while the focus begins a deliberate, smooth shift deeper into the room. With the focus now firmly locked on the background, the vibrant family dinner comes alive. The man in the dark navy blue long-sleeved shirt on the left leans forward, his mouth moving animatedly in a silent exchange. The young girl in the crisp white short-sleeved t-shirt beside him smiles brightly, looking toward the center of the table. The woman on the far left, wearing a soft light blue long-sleeved blouse, turns her head slightly, smiling gently. Across the table, the woman in the light grey button-down shirt smiles broadly, her eyes crinkling, as she rests her hands near her plate. directors.name: James Cameron
directors.notes:
The camera is mounted and travelling — it rides with the body or the machine rather than observing them, and it finishes a move on a different part of the space from the one it started on. Reach first for Tracking Shot, Push In, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pull Out, Arc Shot, Pedestal Up, Pedestal Down and Shake Strongly; leave Static Shot and the rolls alone.
Frame wide enough that the space and the hardware in it read as large against the person, and tighten onto a face only at the moment a decision gets made. Low angles, letting a structure loom over whoever is under it.
Light with hard sources that exist inside the frame — work lamps, flares, screens, fire — carving figures out of a cold cyan-blue ambient, with atmosphere thick enough that a beam has a shape in the air, and one warm amber source somewhere against the blue.
Spend the description on the mechanism: what a thing is made of, what is bolted to what, the readout, the water, the load a surface is taking. Then the face, at the point where the person decides.
Bodies show competence under load. They brace, grip, take weight and keep working, and the effort shows in the hands and the jaw before it reaches the voice. Delivery is clipped, functional, and pitched slightly too loud for the room.
The room is close mechanical detail over a low pressurised bed — servo, hydraulic, metal under stress, water moving as mass — with its own hum continuing underneath all of it. The music is full orchestra with one solo instrument carrying the line above it, percussion entering under the movement, a wide dynamic range, building across a long sustained rise instead of arriving already loud.

directors.name: Quentin Tarantino
directors.notes:
The camera sits still and keeps holding after the action in the shot has finished. When it does move it starts abruptly, travels fast and stops dead instead of easing out. Reach first for Static Shot, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Tilt Down and POV; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals and the shakes alone.
Frame flat and frontal while people talk, from a lens height that is either eye level or startlingly low, looking up from below the tabletop. An insert is enormous relative to the thing it shows.
Light from ordinary sources — daylight through a window, tungsten in a room, the flat fluorescent of a public interior — but the colour off them is rich and heavily saturated: deep reds, hot yellows, warm browns, blacks that stay warm. Surfaces are worn, greasy and used, lit so the wear reads as colour rather than as grime.
Point the camera at hands, feet and footwear, the object on the table, what somebody is eating, the thing being carried, the boot of a car — and a face kept in frame after it has stopped speaking.
People talk at length about small unrelated things, relaxed and unhurried, then stop mid-thought and change tone inside a single beat. Delivery is easy and conversational until it drops flat and quiet.
The room is dry and close — a chair on a hard floor, cutlery, a hard-soled step, the exact mechanical sound an object makes as it is picked up and set down, very little air in it. The music is source-flavoured rather than orchestral: reverb-heavy surf guitar, a soul rhythm section, spaghetti-western brass, an isolated whistled line, holding one tempo and one volume from start to finish with no swell under the action.

directors.name: Wes Anderson
directors.notes:
The camera sits dead centre and moves only along a rigid axis — a fast flat pivot to the next arrangement, a straight lateral, or a straight advance. It never curves and never comes off the horizontal. Reach first for Static Shot, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Zoom In, Tilt Down and Push In; leave Arc Shot, Tracking Shot, the shakes, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame in one-point perspective, perfectly symmetrical, the subject centred and square to the lens looking very nearly down the barrel. An insert is a flat overhead plan view of objects laid out in a row.
Light evenly and almost shadowlessly, high key, with no source doing anything dramatic. A small closed palette of related saturated colours — buttery yellows, pinks, faded reds, sage — against a pale ground.
Point the camera at things that were arranged on purpose: labelled objects, printed matter, the contents of a container, a hand presenting an item flat to the lens, an itemised row of possessions.
Performance is deadpan and upright. Bodies are held square and still, heads turn on the horizontal, and feeling is said out loud instead of shown. Delivery is flat and quick, evenly paced, with no emphasis on any word.
The room is clean and slightly stylised — a small number of specific isolated sounds, each one distinct, over a quiet and almost neutral room tone. The music is plucked strings, harpsichord or celesta playing a brisk repeated figure at a fixed tempo held steady throughout, or one unaccompanied acoustic guitar.

directors.name: Denis Villeneuve
directors.notes:
The camera stays still for a long time, and when it moves it travels in one continuous motion at a constant slow rate from the start of the move to the end of it. Reach first for Static Shot, Push In, Pull Out, Pedestal Up, Pedestal Down, Tilt Up, Arc Shot and Tracking Shot; leave the zooms, the shakes, the rolls and the pans alone.
Frame the extreme wide where a figure is a small mark against the mass of the thing behind it, cut against a face filling the frame with nothing legible behind it. Nothing in the middle.
Light with one hard directional source through a great deal of atmosphere — dust, fog, particulate — so the light has volume. Reduce the frame nearly to a single hue at a time, ochre or slate or near-black, and let figures go to silhouette against a bright void.
Spend the description on mass and scale — the surface of a structure, the distance to a horizon, how much empty space surrounds a body — and then a face, small in the frame, with the rest of the frame empty.
Performance is withheld. Bodies move slowly and deliberately, hold still for a long time before acting, and give almost nothing away. Delivery is quiet, low and unhurried, often barely above the room.
The room is enormous low-frequency air: wind across open ground, a long decay on every impact, and real near-silence between events rather than a bed filling the gaps. The music is a sustained low drone with brass swelling out of it at a very slow tempo and no discernible melody, instruments added one at a time, the volume rising continuously to the end.

directors.name: Kathryn Bigelow
directors.notes:
The camera is carried and reacting rather than planned — it finds the subject a beat late, corrects, and gets jostled by what is happening beside it. It stands among the people in the scene rather than apart from them. Reach first for Shake Slightly, Shake Strongly, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pan Left, Pan Right, Push In and POV; leave Arc Shot, the rolls and Static Shot alone.
Frame on a long lens from a real distance, so the frame is cropped tight and partly blocked by whatever sits between the camera and the subject. The subject falls wherever it happens to fall, often off-centre and part-cut by the frame edge.
Light with whatever the location actually has and nothing added — flat overcast daylight, dust-bleached sun, one work light, night lit only by what somebody switched on. The colour is drained rather than rich: greys, dust, washed blue-white, no warmth put back anywhere and no source arranged to flatter anything.
Point the camera at procedure: the sequence of actions a trained person performs, equipment being used correctly, hands doing a specific technical job, and the periphery being scanned for what is about to happen.
Performance is professional and unglamorous. People do a job under stress, and effort and fear show as breathing and small errors rather than as expression. Delivery is terse, overlapping and functional.
The room is immediate and unmixed — breathing inside the frame, gear and fabric, sharp transient impacts with no tail, and a background that keeps intruding on the foreground. The music is very quiet and very sparse: one low sustained tone, or a dry percussive pulse at a steady unchanging rate, mixed below the sound of the room.

directors.name: Wong Kar-wai
directors.notes:
The camera watches from just outside the moment, low and close, drifting slowly sideways past whatever is in the way, and never repositions for a clear view. Reach first for Static Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Push In, Pan Left, Pan Right and Tilt Down; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals, Shake Strongly and the rolls alone.
Frame tight and obstructed — taken through a doorway, a grille, a mirror or the back of someone's head, with a foreground object cutting into a third of the frame and the subject pushed to the edge of it.
Light in saturated practical colour at night: neon and signage bleeding into the air, tungsten pools, jade green and deep red against black, a smear of light around every source and no even fill anywhere.
Point the camera at repeated intimate detail — a cigarette, a clock, a sleeve, steam coming off food, a hand not quite touching another one — and at the small distance between two people who are not looking at each other.
People stand very close together and do not touch. A hand lifts partway and comes back down. Movements start late and finish slowly, and delivery is soft, quiet and aimed slightly away from whoever it was meant for.
The room keeps the intimate layer close and the world muffled behind it — a fan, rain on an awning, distant traffic, crockery in another room, all of it slightly too far away. The music is one instrument carrying a short melody that repeats without developing — solo strings, a plucked guitar, a slow Latin waltz — at a fixed unhurried tempo, the same figure repeating from beginning to end at one volume.

directors.name: Steven Spielberg
directors.notes:
The camera advances steadily onto whoever is seeing something and keeps advancing after they have registered it — the move ends on a face rather than on the thing that caused it. Reach first for Push In, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pedestal Up, Tilt Up, Arc Shot and Pull Out; leave Shake Strongly, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame at eye level or slightly below, so the world reads at the height of whoever is smallest in the scene. A clean wide that holds the whole group, then a slow tightening onto one reaction inside it.
Light with a strong warm source from behind or beside the subject, throwing a visible shaft through haze or dust, edges rimmed bright, faces lifted by a soft bounce, and the source often flaring straight into the lens.
Point the camera at the reaction rather than the cause — what a face does at the moment it understands, a group turning together, a small object held out on an open palm. The thing itself is frequently kept out of frame.
Performance is readable and unguarded. Wonder, fear and recognition arrive on the face fully and without irony; bodies lean in, reach out, take a step forward. Delivery is warm and overlapping, and people talk over each other.
The room has layered naturalistic depth — the near sound, the middle-distance activity and a real horizon behind them — with the specific sound of the thing being reacted to arriving before it is seen. The music is a full orchestra carrying one clear melodic line on strings or a solo horn, which plays through in full at least once, rises, and lands resolved.

Reach first for Shake Slightly, Shake Strongly, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pan Left, Pan Right, Push In and POV; leave Arc Shot, the rolls and Static Shot alone.
Frame on a long lens from a real distance, so the frame is cropped tight and partly blocked by whatever sits between the camera and the subject. The subject falls wherever it happens to fall, often off-centre and part-cut by the frame edge.
Light with whatever the location actually has and nothing added — flat overcast daylight, dust-bleached sun, one work light, night lit only by what somebody switched on. The colour is drained rather than rich: greys, dust, washed blue-white, no warmth put back anywhere and no source arranged to flatter anything.
Point the camera at procedure: the sequence of actions a trained person performs, equipment being used correctly, hands doing a specific technical job, and the periphery being scanned for what is about to happen.
Performance is professional and unglamorous. People do a job under stress, and effort and fear show as breathing and small errors rather than as expression. Delivery is terse, overlapping and functional.
The room is immediate and unmixed — breathing inside the frame, gear and fabric, sharp transient impacts with no tail, and a background that keeps intruding on the foreground. The music is very quiet and very sparse: one low sustained tone, or a dry percussive pulse at a steady unchanging rate, mixed below the sound of the room.

directors.name: Wong Kar-wai
directors.notes:
The camera watches from just outside the moment, low and close, drifting slowly sideways past whatever is in the way, and never repositions for a clear view. Reach first for Static Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Push In, Pan Left, Pan Right and Tilt Down; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals, Shake Strongly and the rolls alone.
Frame tight and obstructed — taken through a doorway, a grille, a mirror or the back of someone's head, with a foreground object cutting into a third of the frame and the subject pushed to the edge of it.
Light in saturated practical colour at night: neon and signage bleeding into the air, tungsten pools, jade green and deep red against black, a smear of light around every source and no even fill anywhere.
Point the camera at repeated intimate detail — a cigarette, a clock, a sleeve, steam coming off food, a hand not quite touching another one — and at the small distance between two people who are not looking at each other.
People stand very close together and do not touch. A hand lifts partway and comes back down. Movements start late and finish slowly, and delivery is soft, quiet and aimed slightly away from whoever it was meant for.
The room keeps the intimate layer close and the world muffled behind it — a fan, rain on an awning, distant traffic, crockery in another room, all of it slightly too far away. The music is one instrument carrying a short melody that repeats without developing — solo strings, a plucked guitar, a slow Latin waltz — at a fixed unhurried tempo, the same figure repeating from beginning to end at one volume.

directors.name: Steven Spielberg
directors.notes:
The camera advances steadily onto whoever is seeing something and keeps advancing after they have registered it — the move ends on a face rather than on the thing that caused it. Reach first for Push In, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pedestal Up, Tilt Up, Arc Shot and Pull Out; leave Shake Strongly, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame at eye level or slightly below, so the world reads at the height of whoever is smallest in the scene. A clean wide that holds the whole group, then a slow tightening onto one reaction inside it.
Light with a strong warm source from behind or beside the subject, throwing a visible shaft through haze or dust, edges rimmed bright, faces lifted by a soft bounce, and the source often flaring straight into the lens.
Point the camera at the reaction rather than the cause — what a face does at the moment it understands, a group turning together, a small object held out on an open palm. The thing itself is frequently kept out of frame.
Performance is readable and unguarded. Wonder, fear and recognition arrive on the face fully and without irony; bodies lean in, reach out, take a step forward. Delivery is warm and overlapping, and people talk over each other.
The room has layered naturalistic depth — the near sound, the middle-distance activity and a real horizon behind them — with the specific sound of the thing being reacted to arriving before it is seen. The music is a full orchestra carrying one clear melodic line on strings or a solo horn, which plays through in full at least once, rises, and lands resolved.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. directors.name: James Cameron
directors.notes:
The camera is mounted and travelling — it rides with the body or the machine rather than observing them, and it finishes a move on a different part of the space from the one it started on. Reach first for Tracking Shot, Push In, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pull Out, Arc Shot, Pedestal Up, Pedestal Down and Shake Strongly; leave Static Shot and the rolls alone.
Frame wide enough that the space and the hardware in it read as large against the person, and tighten onto a face only at the moment a decision gets made. Low angles, letting a structure loom over whoever is under it.
Light with hard sources that exist inside the frame — work lamps, flares, screens, fire — carving figures out of a cold cyan-blue ambient, with atmosphere thick enough that a beam has a shape in the air, and one warm amber source somewhere against the blue.
Spend the description on the mechanism: what a thing is made of, what is bolted to what, the readout, the water, the load a surface is taking. Then the face, at the point where the person decides.
Bodies show competence under load. They brace, grip, take weight and keep working, and the effort shows in the hands and the jaw before it reaches the voice. Delivery is clipped, functional, and pitched slightly too loud for the room.
The room is close mechanical detail over a low pressurised bed — servo, hydraulic, metal under stress, water moving as mass — with its own hum continuing underneath all of it. The music is full orchestra with one solo instrument carrying the line above it, percussion entering under the movement, a wide dynamic range, building across a long sustained rise instead of arriving already loud.

directors.name: Quentin Tarantino
directors.notes:
The camera sits still and keeps holding after the action in the shot has finished. When it does move it starts abruptly, travels fast and stops dead instead of easing out. Reach first for Static Shot, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Tilt Down and POV; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals and the shakes alone.
Frame flat and frontal while people talk, from a lens height that is either eye level or startlingly low, looking up from below the tabletop. An insert is enormous relative to the thing it shows.
Light from ordinary sources — daylight through a window, tungsten in a room, the flat fluorescent of a public interior — but the colour off them is rich and heavily saturated: deep reds, hot yellows, warm browns, blacks that stay warm. Surfaces are worn, greasy and used, lit so the wear reads as colour rather than as grime.
Point the camera at hands, feet and footwear, the object on the table, what somebody is eating, the thing being carried, the boot of a car — and a face kept in frame after it has stopped speaking.
People talk at length about small unrelated things, relaxed and unhurried, then stop mid-thought and change tone inside a single beat. Delivery is easy and conversational until it drops flat and quiet.
The room is dry and close — a chair on a hard floor, cutlery, a hard-soled step, the exact mechanical sound an object makes as it is picked up and set down, very little air in it. The music is source-flavoured rather than orchestral: reverb-heavy surf guitar, a soul rhythm section, spaghetti-western brass, an isolated whistled line, holding one tempo and one volume from start to finish with no swell under the action.

directors.name: Wes Anderson
directors.notes:
The camera sits dead centre and moves only along a rigid axis — a fast flat pivot to the next arrangement, a straight lateral, or a straight advance. It never curves and never comes off the horizontal. Reach first for Static Shot, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Zoom In, Tilt Down and Push In; leave Arc Shot, Tracking Shot, the shakes, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame in one-point perspective, perfectly symmetrical, the subject centred and square to the lens looking very nearly down the barrel. An insert is a flat overhead plan view of objects laid out in a row.
Light evenly and almost shadowlessly, high key, with no source doing anything dramatic. A small closed palette of related saturated colours — buttery yellows, pinks, faded reds, sage — against a pale ground.
Point the camera at things that were arranged on purpose: labelled objects, printed matter, the contents of a container, a hand presenting an item flat to the lens, an itemised row of possessions.
Performance is deadpan and upright. Bodies are held square and still, heads turn on the horizontal, and feeling is said out loud instead of shown. Delivery is flat and quick, evenly paced, with no emphasis on any word.
The room is clean and slightly stylised — a small number of specific isolated sounds, each one distinct, over a quiet and almost neutral room tone. The music is plucked strings, harpsichord or celesta playing a brisk repeated figure at a fixed tempo held steady throughout, or one unaccompanied acoustic guitar.

directors.name: Denis Villeneuve
directors.notes:
The camera stays still for a long time, and when it moves it travels in one continuous motion at a constant slow rate from the start of the move to the end of it. Reach first for Static Shot, Push In, Pull Out, Pedestal Up, Pedestal Down, Tilt Up, Arc Shot and Tracking Shot; leave the zooms, the shakes, the rolls and the pans alone.
Frame the extreme wide where a figure is a small mark against the mass of the thing behind it, cut against a face filling the frame with nothing legible behind it. Nothing in the middle.
Light with one hard directional source through a great deal of atmosphere — dust, fog, particulate — so the light has volume. Reduce the frame nearly to a single hue at a time, ochre or slate or near-black, and let figures go to silhouette against a bright void.
Spend the description on mass and scale — the surface of a structure, the distance to a horizon, how much empty space surrounds a body — and then a face, small in the frame, with the rest of the frame empty.
Performance is withheld. Bodies move slowly and deliberately, hold still for a long time before acting, and give almost nothing away. Delivery is quiet, low and unhurried, often barely above the room.
The room is enormous low-frequency air: wind across open ground, a long decay on every impact, and real near-silence between events rather than a bed filling the gaps. The music is a sustained low drone with brass swelling out of it at a very slow tempo and no discernible melody, instruments added one at a time, the volume rising continuously to the end.

directors.name: Kathryn Bigelow
directors.notes:
The camera is carried and reacting rather than planned — it finds the subject a beat late, corrects, and gets jostled by what is happening beside it. It stands among the people in the scene rather than apart from them. Reach first for Shake Slightly, Shake Strongly, Tracking Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pan Left, Pan Right, Push In and POV; leave Arc Shot, the rolls and Static Shot alone.
Frame on a long lens from a real distance, so the frame is cropped tight and partly blocked by whatever sits between the camera and the subject. The subject falls wherever it happens to fall, often off-centre and part-cut by the frame edge.
Light with whatever the location actually has and nothing added — flat overcast daylight, dust-bleached sun, one work light, night lit only by what somebody switched on. The colour is drained rather than rich: greys, dust, washed blue-white, no warmth put back anywhere and no source arranged to flatter anything.
Point the camera at procedure: the sequence of actions a trained person performs, equipment being used correctly, hands doing a specific technical job, and the periphery being scanned for what is about to happen.
Performance is professional and unglamorous. People do a job under stress, and effort and fear show as breathing and small errors rather than as expression. Delivery is terse, overlapping and functional.
The room is immediate and unmixed — breathing inside the frame, gear and fabric, sharp transient impacts with no tail, and a background that keeps intruding on the foreground. The music is very quiet and very sparse: one low sustained tone, or a dry percussive pulse at a steady unchanging rate, mixed below the sound of the room.

directors.name: Wong Kar-wai
directors.notes:
The camera watches from just outside the moment, low and close, drifting slowly sideways past whatever is in the way, and never repositions for a clear view. Reach first for Static Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Push In, Pan Left, Pan Right and Tilt Down; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals, Shake Strongly and the rolls alone.
Frame tight and obstructed — taken through a doorway, a grille, a mirror or the back of someone's head, with a foreground object cutting into a third of the frame and the subject pushed to the edge of it.
Light in saturated practical colour at night: neon and signage bleeding into the air, tungsten pools, jade green and deep red against black, a smear of light around every source and no even fill anywhere.
Point the camera at repeated intimate detail — a cigarette, a clock, a sleeve, steam coming off food, a hand not quite touching another one — and at the small distance between two people who are not looking at each other.
People stand very close together and do not touch. A hand lifts partway and comes back down. Movements start late and finish slowly, and delivery is soft, quiet and aimed slightly away from whoever it was meant for.
The room keeps the intimate layer close and the world muffled behind it — a fan, rain on an awning, distant traffic, crockery in another room, all of it slightly too far away. The music is one instrument carrying a short melody that repeats without developing — solo strings, a plucked guitar, a slow Latin waltz — at a fixed unhurried tempo, the same figure repeating from beginning to end at one volume.

directors.name: Steven Spielberg
directors.notes:

handpainted-anim-v2.name: Hand-Painted Animation
handpainted-anim-v2.body:
## What it's for

Soft hand-painted animation: visible brush texture, watercolour backgrounds with bloomed edges,
warm daylight, gentle character motion with follow-through. Good for pastoral scenes, weather,
food, quiet character moments, anything where the appeal is in the painted surface rather than
in detail density.

## When NOT to use it

Not for anything that needs photographic skin, legible small text, hard mechanical edges, or
fast action — the painted texture smears under speed and the model loses fine geometry. Do not
stack it with a photoreal style LoRA; the two fight and the result reads as neither.

## Strength guidance

0.4–0.6 keeps recognisable faces and adds only the surface treatment. 0.7–0.9 is the intended
look. Above 0.9 backgrounds start to dissolve into wash and thin objects disappear.

## Known failure modes

Small on-screen text becomes unreadable — which matters more here than it would at 2K, because
local output is 768p on the short edge and there is no regeneration stage to recover glyphs.
Hands at rest are fine; hands manipulating small objects lose finger separation.

## Example style openings

Ref2VA, as the first item of the style line:

    The target video is in hndpntd_anim_v2 hand-painted animation style with soft watercolour
    backgrounds and warm afternoon light.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

json.reasoning: No source reference or explicit rendering-style request is supplied. The intent describes only scene action and a cut, which does not specify a rendering medium, style phrase, or compatible treatment.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

director.name: James Cameron
director.notes:
The camera is mounted and travelling — it rides with the body or the machine rather than observing them, and it finishes a move on a different part of the space from the one it started on. Reach first for Tracking Shot, Push In, Truck Left, Truck Right, Pull Out, Arc Shot, Pedestal Up, Pedestal Down and Shake Strongly; leave Static Shot and the rolls alone.
Frame wide enough that the space and the hardware in it read as large against the person, and tighten onto a face only at the moment a decision gets made. Low angles, letting a structure loom over whoever is under it.
Light with hard sources that exist inside the frame — work lamps, flares, screens, fire — carving figures out of a cold cyan-blue ambient, with atmosphere thick enough that a beam has a shape in the air, and one warm amber source somewhere against the blue.
Spend the description on the mechanism: what a thing is made of, what is bolted to what, the readout, the water, the load a surface is taking. Then the face, at the point where the person decides.
Bodies show competence under load. They brace, grip, take weight and keep working, and the effort shows in the hands and the jaw before it reaches the voice. Delivery is clipped, functional, and pitched slightly too loud for the room.
The room is close mechanical detail over a low pressurised bed — servo, hydraulic, metal under stress, water moving as mass — with its own hum continuing underneath all of it. The music is full orchestra with one solo instrument carrying the line above it, percussion entering under the movement, a wide dynamic range, building across a long sustained rise instead of arriving already loud.

director.name: Quentin Tarantino
director.notes:
The camera sits still and keeps holding after the action in the shot has finished. When it does move it starts abruptly, travels fast and stops dead instead of easing out. Reach first for Static Shot, Zoom In, Zoom Out, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Tilt Down and POV; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals and the shakes alone.
Frame flat and frontal while people talk, from a lens height that is either eye level or startlingly low, looking up from below the tabletop. An insert is enormous relative to the thing it shows.
Light from ordinary sources — daylight through a window, tungsten in a room, the flat fluorescent of a public interior — but the colour off them is rich and heavily saturated: deep reds, hot yellows, warm browns, blacks that stay warm. Surfaces are worn, greasy and used, lit so the wear reads as colour rather than as grime.
Point the camera at hands, feet and footwear, the object on the table, what somebody is eating, the thing being carried, the boot of a car — and a face kept in frame after it has stopped speaking.
People talk at length about small unrelated things, relaxed and unhurried, then stop mid-thought and change tone inside a single beat. Delivery is easy and conversational until it drops flat and quiet.
The room is dry and close — a chair on a hard floor, cutlery, a hard-soled step, the exact mechanical sound an object makes as it is picked up and set down, very little air in it. The music is source-flavoured rather than orchestral: reverb-heavy surf guitar, a soul rhythm section, spaghetti-western brass, an isolated whistled line, holding one tempo and one volume from start to finish with no swell under the action.

director.name: Wes Anderson
director.notes:
The camera sits dead centre and moves only along a rigid axis — a fast flat pivot to the next arrangement, a straight lateral, or a straight advance. It never curves and never comes off the horizontal. Reach first for Static Shot, Pan Left, Pan Right, Truck Left, Truck Right, Zoom In, Tilt Down and Push In; leave Arc Shot, Tracking Shot, the shakes, the rolls and POV alone.
Frame in one-point perspective, perfectly symmetrical, the subject centred and square to the lens looking very nearly down the barrel. An insert is a flat overhead plan view of objects laid out in a row.
Light evenly and almost shadowlessly, high key, with no source doing anything dramatic. A small closed palette of related saturated colours — buttery yellows, pinks, faded reds, sage — against a pale ground.
Point the camera at things that were arranged on purpose: labelled objects, printed matter, the contents of a container, a hand presenting an item flat to the lens, an itemised row of possessions.
Performance is deadpan and upright. Bodies are held square and still, heads turn on the horizontal, and feeling is said out loud instead of shown. Delivery is flat and quick, evenly paced, with no emphasis on any word.
The room is clean and slightly stylised — a small number of specific isolated sounds, each one distinct, over a quiet and almost neutral room tone. The music is plucked strings, harpsichord or celesta playing a brisk repeated figure at a fixed tempo held steady throughout, or one unaccompanied acoustic guitar.

director.notes:

director.name: Wong Kar-wai
director.notes:
The camera watches from just outside the moment, low and close, drifting slowly sideways past whatever is in the way, and never repositions for a clear view. Reach first for Static Shot, Truck Left, Truck Right, Push In, Pan Left, Pan Right and Tilt Down; leave Arc Shot, the pedestals, Shake Strongly and the rolls alone.
Frame tight and obstructed — taken through a doorway, a grille, a mirror or the back of someone's head, with a foreground object cutting into a third of the frame and the subject pushed to the edge of it.
Light in saturated practical colour at night: neon and signage bleeding into the air, tungsten pools, jade green and deep red against black, a smear of light around every source and no even fill anywhere.
Point the camera at repeated intimate detail — a cigarette, a clock, a sleeve, steam coming off food, a hand not quite touching another one — and at the small distance between two people who are not looking at each other.
People stand very close together and do not touch. A hand lifts partway and comes back down. Movements start late and finish slowly, and delivery is soft, quiet and aimed slightly away from whoever it was meant for.
The room keeps the intimate layer close and the world muffled behind it — a fan, rain on an awning, distant traffic, crockery in another room, all of it slightly too far away. The music is one instrument carrying a short melody that repeats without developing — solo strings, a plucked guitar, a slow Latin waltz — at a fixed unhurried tempo, the same figure repeating from beginning to end at one volume.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve only whether the caller authorizes departing from an attached visual reference's rendering. You receive no source look, taxonomy, target geometry or director: none can grant permission. Read the complete caller request and constraints.
Choose rendering_transformation when the caller expressly asks to transform/reinterpret/restyle the rendering, with an authorizing operation and its target. Choose target_rendition when a grammatical instruction directly specifies the result's rendering in a target style or medium, even without a separate transformation verb. Choose preserve when no such instruction exists. A detached adjective or noun-phrase style tag appended to scene action is descriptive metadata, not a rendering operation or a complete target-rendition directive. A fragment does not become authoritative simply because it has its own sentence punctuation. Do not treat every style mention as authorization.
Interpret grammatical and semantic relationships, not keyword lists. A rendering operation can target a technique of unknown taxonomy and can stay within the same coarse family as the source. A change in depicted subject, motion, setting, dreamlike content or mood alone is not a rendering conversion. For an authorized instruction, operation_quote is its exact complete authorizing caller phrase and target is the complete requested rendition noun phrase. For preserve, operation_quote and target must be empty. Return only typed JSON. Do not infer what the unseen reference looks like.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.

Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.

Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.
