With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.

Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve only whether the caller authorizes departing from an attached visual reference's rendering. You receive no source look, taxonomy, target geometry or director: none can grant permission. Read the complete caller request and constraints.
Choose rendering_transformation when the caller expressly asks to transform/reinterpret/restyle the rendering, with an authorizing operation and its target. Choose target_rendition when a grammatical instruction directly specifies the result's rendering in a target style or medium, even without a separate transformation verb. Choose preserve when no such instruction exists. A detached adjective or noun-phrase style tag appended to scene action is descriptive metadata, not a rendering operation or a complete target-rendition directive. A fragment does not become authoritative simply because it has its own sentence punctuation. Do not treat every style mention as authorization.
Interpret grammatical and semantic relationships, not keyword lists. A rendering operation can target a technique of unknown taxonomy and can stay within the same coarse family as the source. A change in depicted subject, motion, setting, dreamlike content or mood alone is not a rendering conversion. For an authorized instruction, operation_quote is its exact complete authorizing caller phrase and target is the complete requested rendition noun phrase. For preserve, operation_quote and target must be empty. Return only typed JSON. Do not infer what the unseen reference looks like.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

If identity/wardrobe is unchanged, descriptor_source=reference and descriptor equals the exact source descriptor, target_mention/request_quote empty, claims/requested_attributes/adjusted_attributes empty. A mixed attribute containing a stable physical fact and view packaging MUST retain its exact source in retained_attributes and use adjusted_attributes kind=presentation_cleanup to preserve the stable fact while removing only the view packaging. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

recorded_request.system:
Classify rendering-family IDs, compatible treatments and the requested style phrase. rendering_permission already settles authorization without knowing the reference look: its disposition, operation_quote and target are host-owned schema constants. Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Treatments are the supplied compatible treatment vocabulary, in the order the user asks for them; never classify a medium such as anime as a treatment. Return only JSON. Do not invent explicit instructions or scan from a keyword list.

recorded_request.system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

Copy them exactly and NEVER re-author that permission based on a source/target taxonomy mismatch, equal buckets or a loose style mention. No source mismatch grants departure. A deliberate authorized transformation can stay within one coarse family. With no medium-governing visual reference, disposition is no_reference; explicit structured Style remains the requested style phrase.
A theme, atmosphere, physical impossibility or imagined subject matter does not specify a rendering process. Unknown technique/family is empty, rather than guessed animation or painting from unusual content. A requested target can be valid while its rendering family remains unknown. Keep the complete requested rendering noun phrase in requested_style even when requested_medium is empty; absence of a coarse family never erases a named visual rendition. Motion does not by itself change rendering family. requested_style can record an unlicensed descriptive medium mention, while the separate permission still preserves the reference. Do not copy source-medium words into the requested family merely because they conflict.
reference_medium and requested_medium are the supplied semantic taxonomy IDs; unknown is empty. 2d-animation includes flat or digitally drawn illustration, comic/graphic illustration and hand-drawn or cel animation, whether realistic or stylised. painted denotes a work presented as physical painted media, with painterly brushwork/paint surface; it is not a catch-all for every illustrated reference. 3d-animation denotes volumetric computer-rendered animation; stop-motion denotes photographed physical miniature/puppet frame animation. archival denotes an explicitly analog film-stock or historical monochrome film rendering process, including the texture and tonal reproduction of such capture; ordinary contemporary photographic depiction is live-action. A purely monochrome treatment without a specified capture process can have an unknown family while still having a nonempty requested_style. A still illustration may belong to an animation rendering family without making any claim that the attached still itself moves. Use the identified rendering process, not incidental words or whether a drawing is semi-realistic. Reference style comes from the edit-source clip before an incoming replacement/placement portrait, otherwise the first observed image style. Classify that actual observed phrase, never a guessed scene. When the schema includes retained_style, the selected source is a reference sheet: return only its actual rendering medium and stylistic traits, excluding sheet/turnaround/panel/label/contact-sheet/presentation packaging. That cleanup applies ONLY to content references. An actual_frame reference has the opposite obligation: its full original image, including any sheet panels, labels and backdrop, is the actual anchored target frame; never remove those elements or substitute a hero crop. Preserve its original observed style phrase when no rendering change is authorized. If the observed style phrase contains no presentation packaging, copy its existing wording exactly; otherwise remove only that packaging, keeping all actual visual style. No invented restyling. Requested medium records even a loose mentioned medium, while disposition independently decides whether it is authorized. requested_style is the complete requested rendering noun phrase, excluding separately listed compatible treatments; it includes a named rendition whose process is outside or less specific than the coarse taxonomy. Leave it empty only if there is no requested rendering phrase. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.
